metadata.scope: All 14 belt profiles in pulley-generator.scad: MXL, 40DP, XL, H, T2.5, T5, T10, AT5, HTD 3mm, HTD 5mm, HTD 8mm, GT2 2mm, GT2 3mm, GT2 5mm. Also includes: GT2 2mm smooth bearing idler pulley (standalone — not from pulley-generator.scad).

pulley3DP.purpose: Simplified helper for 3D-printable pulleys with hardcoded sensible defaults.

pulleyCAD.purpose: CAD-representation helper. Auto-calculates retainer/idler offsets to hit exact pulleyDiameter.

pulley.purpose: Full parametric pulley — every section independently controlled.

optional_parameters.toothWidthTweak: Added to belt tooth width model. 0.2 mm typical for 3D printing. Positive value makes pulley teeth narrower (looser fit).
optional_parameters.toothDepthTweak: Added to belt tooth depth. Changes tooth shape — use sparingly.
optional_parameters.autoFlip: Flips assembly if teeth+idler OD > base diameter, for flat print bed face.

pulleyBase.purpose: Hub cylinder only. Auto-bevels top edge when base > upperSection by up to 1 mm.

captiveGrubAndNut.purpose: Nut pocket negative volume — subtract from base in difference().

pulleyData.note: pulley_OD is the solid cylinder OD before teeth are subtracted. The library builds the tooth section by starting with this cylinder, then cutting tooth-shaped polygon profiles (polyPoints) once per tooth around the circumference.

calc_pulley_dia_tooth_spacing_curvefit.note: Curve-fit accounts for effective pitch variation with tooth count in trapezoidal profiles.

geometry_model.axis: Z — shaft bore runs along Z; pulley spins about Z.
assembly_order_bottom_to_top: base (pulleyBase)      — widest hub cylinder; captive nuts + shaft bore
idler (pulleyIdler)    — tapered+flat flange below teeth; retains belt from falling off downward
teeth (pulleyTeeth)   — toothed cylinder; teeth are SUBTRACTIVE grooves from solid cylinder
retainer (pulleyRetainer) — tapered+flat flange above teeth; retains belt from riding up
geometry_model.tooth_geometry: SUBTRACTIVE. Library starts with solid cylinder at pulley_OD/2, then cuts polyPoints polygon profile (belt tooth shape) once per tooth. Belt rubber teeth interlock into these grooves.
geometry_model.shaft_bore: Subtracted through full assembly height with cylinder(r=shaftDiameter/2). Extends 1mm below base and 1mm above retainer.
geometry_model.captive_nut: Nut pocket placed at baseHeight/2 inside base cylinder. offsetFromShaft in captiveNuts[2] is added to shaftDiameter/2 internally by the library.

constraint_checks.message: Base height must be >= nut face size or captive nuts won't fit.
Base diameter too small for nut depth — increase baseDiameter.
Unsupported model — pulleyData() returns [] and library echoes UNSUPPORTED MODEL.

output_policy.openscad_code: Use include <pulley-generator.scad> ONLY for toothed/timing pulleys that call pulley3DP(), pulley(), pulleyCAD(), pulleyTeeth(), pulleyRetainer(), pulleyIdler(), pulleyBase(), or captiveGrubAndNut(). DO NOT use include for smooth bearing idlers such as 623ZZ, 624ZZ, 625ZZ, or 608ZZ idlers. Smooth bearing idlers must be generated as standalone OpenSCAD primitives using cylinder(), union(), difference(), and translate().

priority_order: If prompt contains smooth + idler, bearing idler, 624ZZ, 623ZZ, 625ZZ, 608ZZ, bearing sleeve, free spinning pulley, or belt tensioner idler, classify as smooth_bearing_idler.
If prompt contains teeth, tooth count, motor pulley, drive pulley, grub screw, set screw, captive nut, pulley3DP, pulleyCAD, or timing pulley, classify as toothed_timing_pulley.
If prompt contains both GT2 and 624ZZ/idler/smooth/bearing, smooth_bearing_idler wins.

material_suggestions.notes: Best surface finish; anodize for wear resistance.
Self-lubricating; tight tolerances; good belt contact surface.
Best wear resistance for printed parts. Use toothWidthTweak=0.2 and $fn=teethCount*4.
Easier to print than PA12; lower wear resistance. Use toothWidthTweak=0.25.

parts.name: MXL timing pulley

belt_profile_data.application: Light-duty imperial standard (~0.080"). Precision instruments, small desktop CNC, light robotics.

pulley_OD.note: Solid cylinder OD before tooth grooves are subtracted.

totalHeight.formula: baseInfo[1] + idlerInfo[1] + idlerInfo[2] + beltWidth + retainerInfo[1] + retainerInfo[2]

parts.name: 40DP timing pulley

belt_profile_data.application: Imperial diametral pitch. Older US CNC and precision instrument drives.

parts.name: XL timing pulley

belt_profile_data.application: Light-duty imperial 1/5" pitch. Servo drives, older CNC axes, light automation.

parts.name: GT2 2mm smooth bearing idler pulley
intent_rules: Use this record when the prompt contains idler, smooth idler, bearing bore, bearing seat, tensioner pulley, free spinning pulley, or no drive teeth.
Do not add grub screws, set screws, captive nuts, keyed bores, or motor-shaft hubs unless explicitly requested.
An idler pulley rotates freely on a bearing and should use a bearing seat instead of a motor shaft set screw.

parts.name: H timing pulley

belt_profile_data.application: Heavy-duty imperial 3/8" pitch. Industrial machinery, large CNC routers, car timing belt drives.

parts.name: T2.5 timing pulley

belt_profile_data.dia_formula_note: Curve-fit used; effective pitch varies with tooth count in T2.5.
belt_profile_data.application: Older metric CNC, light automation, small servo drives. Trapezoidal profile.

parts.name: T5 timing pulley

belt_profile_data.application: Common metric servo drive belt. Medium-duty automation, stepper motor systems.

parts.name: T10 timing pulley

belt_profile_data.application: Heavy-duty metric 10mm pitch. Industrial conveyors, large CNC gantries, heavy automation.

parts.name: AT5 timing pulley

belt_profile_data.dia_formula_note: Identical OD formula to T5. AT5 has wider tooth (4.268 vs 3.264 mm) for higher back-tension torque capacity.
belt_profile_data.application: Higher torque than T5 at same pitch. One-directional drives, conveyors, automation with significant back-tension.

pulley_OD.note: Same OD as T5 — only tooth width differs in polyPoints.

parts.name: HTD 3mm timing pulley

belt_profile_data.application: HTD (High Torque Drive) 3mm pitch. Robotics, heavy 3D printers, light industrial. Rounded tooth resists tooth shear better than trapezoidal at same pitch.

parts.name: HTD 5mm timing pulley

belt_profile_data.application: Most common HTD size. Heavy-duty CNC, robotics, industrial automation, 3D printer extruders.

parts.name: HTD 8mm timing pulley

belt_profile_data.application: Heaviest HTD variant. Industrial machinery, large robots, high-torque drives requiring maximum belt load capacity.

parts.name: GT2 2mm timing pulley

belt_profile_data.application: Most common for 3D printers, CoreXY, desktop CNC. Anti-backlash rounded profile. Standard 6mm belt width.
belt_profile_data.tooth_geometry_note: Grooves are subtracted from solid cylinder using curvilinear polyPoints profile. Belt rubber teeth mesh into grooves. Groove width is 1.494 mm + toothWidthTweak.

model.note: Exact string — space required between GT2 and 2mm

pulley_OD.note: Solid cylinder diameter before grooves subtracted. NOT the same as pitch diameter.

totalHeight.formula: baseInfo[1] + idlerInfo[1] + idlerInfo[2] + beltWidth + retainerInfo[1] + retainerInfo[2]

toothDistanceFromCentre.note: Used internally by library to position each tooth groove origin.

main_features: toothed cylinder: solid cylinder at pulley_OD/2 radius; GT2 groove profiles subtracted once per tooth around circumference at $fn=teethCount*4
retainer (above teeth): tapered disc — flat base at pulley_OD/2, slopes outward by offset over taperedHeight, then flat at flatHeight
idler (below teeth): tapered disc — same shape inverted, below the tooth section
base: solid cylinder below idler; wider hub; auto-bevels if base > connected section
shaft bore: cylinder at shaftDiameter/2 subtracted through full height from -1mm to retainer top
captive nut pocket: hex/square recess in base wall at baseHeight/2, aimed radially; grub-screw hole also subtracted
design_rules: toothWidthTweak = 0.2 mm is standard starting point for 3D printing — adds clearance to belt groove fit
NEMA17 shaft is 5.0 mm nominal; use shaftDiameter = 5.2 mm for 3D-print bore clearance
baseInfo[1] >= nutProfile[2]: base height must exceed nut face size (5.7 mm for M3 hex)
(baseInfo[0] - shaftDiameter) / 2 >= nutProfile[3] + 3 mm: wall must fit nut depth plus 3mm
autoFlip = true: flips if (pulley_OD + 2*idlerInfo[0]) > baseInfo[0], placing large-face down for FDM
teethCount minimum 16 for GT2 2mm to maintain proper groove engagement and tooth strength
$fn = teethCount*4 is used internally for toothed cylinder — no user action needed

constraint_checks.message: Base height must be >= nut face size (5.7mm for M3 hex).
Base diameter too small for nut depth — increase baseDiameter.
Minimum 16 teeth for GT2 2mm reliable engagement.

parts.name: GT2 3mm timing pulley

belt_profile_data.application: Higher torque than GT2 2mm. Heavy 3D printers, medium-duty CNC, robots needing GT2 anti-backlash with higher power.

parts.name: GT2 5mm timing pulley

belt_profile_data.application: High-torque GT2 variant. Heavy robot arms, large CNC axes, industrial synchronous drives with GT2 anti-backlash at high power.

parts.name: GT2 2mm smooth bearing idler pulley — 6 mm belt
parts.library_note: STANDALONE — does NOT use pulley-generator.scad. This part is a smooth sleeve pressed onto a standard radial ball bearing and mounted on a shoulder bolt or screw. No teeth. No library include required.
parts.description: A smooth cylindrical sleeve pressed onto a ball bearing outer race. The belt runs on the smooth outer surface, which has two raised shoulder flanges to retain the belt axially. The bearing spins freely on a fixed shoulder bolt through the inner bore. Used as a belt guide, tensioner, or direction-change idler in GT2 2mm belt drives.

624ZZ.note: Most common for GT2 6mm belt desktop CNC and 3D printers

608ZZ.note: Large idler for wide belts or high load

parts.recommended_bearing: 624ZZ — bore 4 mm, OD 13 mm, width 5 mm, M4 shoulder bolt

bearing_OD_mm.note: 624ZZ outer diameter — sleeve is pressed onto this

bearing_bore_mm.note: 624ZZ inner bore — shoulder bolt passes through

bearing_width_mm.note: 624ZZ axial width — sleeve height matches this

wall_thickness_mm.note: Sleeve wall over bearing OD. Min 1.0 mm; 1.5 mm recommended for PA12/PETG

flange_overhang_mm.note: Radial height of belt-retention shoulder above belt contact surface

flange_thickness_mm.note: Axial thickness of each retention shoulder disc

press_fit_tol_mm.note: Sleeve inner bore = bearing_OD + press_fit_tol. Negative = interference fit onto bearing OD. For 3D printing use -0.1 to -0.15 mm (plastic expands on cooling)

sleeve_OD.note: Belt contact surface diameter. Keep close to the GT2 2mm toothed pulley OD (~12.22 mm) so belt runs at consistent height, but exact match is not required for an idler.

sleeve_bore.note: Inner bore of printed sleeve. Must be a tight press fit onto bearing OD. Nominal = bearing_OD for machined; bearing_OD - 0.1 to -0.15 for 3D printed (shrinkage gives interference).

sleeve_belt_height.note: Height of the smooth cylindrical belt contact zone — exactly matches belt width.

sleeve_total_height.note: Total axial height of sleeve including both retention flanges.

flange_OD.note: Outer diameter of belt-retention shoulder discs.

bearing_press_depth.note: Sleeve inner bore depth equals bearing width. Bearing seats flush with or recessed 0.2 mm below flange face.

main_features: belt contact cylinder: smooth cylinder at sleeve_OD/2, height = belt_width_mm — NO teeth, NO grooves
bottom retention flange: flat disc at lower end of belt zone, OD = flange_OD, thickness = flange_thickness_mm — prevents belt falling off downward
top retention flange: identical flat disc at upper end of belt zone — prevents belt riding off upward
inner bore: cylindrical hole at sleeve_bore/2 through full sleeve height — tight press fit onto bearing OD
bearing seat: no internal step; bearing presses in from one end to full depth
no shaft bore: the bearing inner race is the bore; sleeve does NOT contact the axle bolt
design_rules: sleeve inner bore = bearing_OD - 0.1 mm (3D print) or bearing_OD - 0.0 / +0.0 (machined interference) — sleeve presses onto bearing OD, NOT onto the bolt
axle bolt passes THROUGH bearing inner bore only — do NOT let bolt shoulder contact sleeve; washer between bolt head/nut and sleeve face
sleeve_OD belt contact surface must be perfectly smooth — no layer lines visible in belt zone; orient print with axis vertical or post-process
flange_thickness >= 1.0 mm to survive belt side loads without shearing at root
flange_overhang >= 1.0 mm to retain GT2 6 mm belt (belt is 6 mm wide, flanges must extend at least 1 mm each side)
wall_thickness >= 1.0 mm over bearing OD to provide adequate press-fit strength; 1.5 mm recommended
sleeve_total_height must not exceed bearing_width_mm + 2.0 mm or sleeve will contact frame before bearing seats
for 624ZZ: sleeve bore = 12.9 mm (3D print) — standard starting point; reduce to 12.85 mm if bearing slips

constraint_checks.message: Sleeve bore must be SMALLER than bearing OD for press fit. sleeve_bore = bearing_OD + press_fit_tol where press_fit_tol is negative.
Sleeve total height must not exceed bearing width + 2 mm or sleeve will bottom on frame before bearing seats.
Wall thickness below 1.0 mm — risk of sleeve splitting during press fit or belt load.
Flange overhang below 1.0 mm — belt may ride off under lateral load.

failure_modes: sleeve bore too large — bearing OD loose in sleeve, rattles under belt load; re-print with bore_tol = -0.15 mm
sleeve bore too small — cannot press bearing in; re-print with bore_tol = -0.05 mm
no flanges or flanges too small — belt walks off axially under any lateral force
belt contact zone has layer lines — belt catches and wears; orient print vertically or sand zone smooth
bolt shoulder contacts sleeve inner face instead of bearing inner race — bearing cannot spin freely; use correct shoulder bolt length
sleeve height > bearing width + 2 mm — sleeve bottoms on frame before bearing seats; sleeve appears loose axially
parts.mounting_note: Use a shoulder bolt whose shoulder diameter = bearing inner bore (4 mm for 624ZZ) and whose shoulder length = bearing_width_mm. Add one flat washer (OD > sleeve_OD) between bolt head and sleeve face, and one between sleeve face and nut/frame, to prevent bolt head/nut from gripping sleeve and locking it.
